title: "Access to API" permission not enforced server-side in user.createApiKey
summary:
## Summary

The per-member "Access to API" toggle (`canAccessToAPI`, resolved as `api: ["read"]`) only hides the API keys UI. `user.createApiKey` is a plain `protectedProcedure` with no permission check, and API-key authentication does not check `api: read` either. A member whose admin has explicitly denied API access can still mint a non-expiring API key and use it.

## Affected version

- Verified on: Dokploy v0.30.10 (self-hosted)
- Code unchanged on `canary` at d64ebedd0

## Code

- `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/user.ts:757-783` (canary): `createApiKey: protectedProcedure`, only checks membership of `metadata.organizationId`.
- `packages/server/src/lib/auth.ts:557-641`: `validateRequest` accepts any valid key; no `api: read` check.
- `api.read` is only consulted in the UI: `apps/dokploy/pages/dashboard/settings/profile.tsx:23`, `apps/dokploy/pages/swagger.tsx:103`.

## Preconditions

- Attacker is a `member` of an organization with "Access to API" disabled (the default for new members).

## Reproduction (local test instance only)

```
# as the member (session cookie); user.getPermissions shows api: {"read": false}
curl -s -b member.jar -H "origin: http://127.0.0.1:13000" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"test","metadata":{"organizationId":"<member org id>"}}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:13000/api/user.createApiKey
# -> {"id":"...","key":"<key>","enabled":true,"expiresAt":null,...}

curl -s -H "x-api-key: <key>" http://127.0.0.1:13000/api/user.get
# -> member record, role "member"
```

## Observed result

- `user.getPermissions` for the member: `api: {"read": false}`.
- `user.createApiKey` succeeded and returned a key with `expiresAt: null`.
- The key authenticated REST calls with the member's permissions (e.g. `user.get`, `server.getServerMetrics`).
- After the member signed out (session cookie now returns Unauthorized), the key still worked.

## Impact

- An admin cannot actually prevent a member from getting programmatic API access.
- The member obtains a long-lived credential that is independent of their session. Using it does not go through the 2FA challenge.
- Not tested: whether turning the toggle off revokes existing keys. From the code, it does not, since `validateRequest` never consults it.

## Suggested fix (tested)

In `user.createApiKey`, after the existing membership check, require `api: read` in the organization the key is bound to (not the caller's active organization, since the key's org comes from `metadata.organizationId`). Owners/admins and members with "Access to API" enabled keep working.

Patch against `canary` d64ebedd0:

```diff
diff --git a/apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/user.ts b/apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/user.ts
index 576548737..218c05ec1 100644
--- a/apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/user.ts
+++ b/apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/user.ts
@@ -34,6 +34,7 @@ import {
 	user,
 } from "@dokploy/server/db/schema";
 import {
+	checkPermission,
 	hasPermission,
 	resolvePermissions,
 } from "@dokploy/server/services/permission";
@@ -772,6 +773,14 @@ export const userRouter = createTRPCRouter({
 						message: "You are not a member of this organization",
 					});
 				}
+
+				await checkPermission(
+					{
+						user: ctx.user,
+						session: { activeOrganizationId: input.metadata.organizationId },
+					},
+					{ api: ["read"] },
+				);
 			}
 
 			const apiKey = await createApiKey(ctx.user.id, input);
```

Verified by building `canary` d64ebedd0 with this patch (together with the fixes from my other reports) and upgrading the vulnerable test instance in place. Typecheck passes for `packages/server` and `apps/dokploy`; the vitest suite shows the same 7 failures with and without the change.

After the fix: the member with "Access to API" off gets `UNAUTHORIZED` from `user.createApiKey`; the owner still creates keys.

Not included in this patch: enforcing `api: read` in `validateRequest`, so revoking the toggle does not disable keys that already exist. Worth considering, but it...
